text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.8% today as oil prices dropped sharply, with US crude sliding to $89.62 a barrel from levels above $140 just days ago. The decline came despite ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iran's escalating attacks on U.S. positions in Kuwait and threats against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz would normally support oil prices, but broader market forces appear to have overwhelmed those safety concerns.

The stock's recent weakness reflects a broader pullback in energy prices over the past week, even as headlines have grown more alarming. When oil prices fall this decisively, it typically pressures integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips regardless of supply-risk premiums, since lower crude undermines both their production revenue and refining margins.
